Former Deputy Finance Minister and Member of Parliament for Nhyaieso, Dr Stephen Amoah, says the National Democratic Congress (NDC) has yet to implement the 24-hour economy it promised Ghanaians ahead of the 2024 general elections.
His comments follow claims by Presidential Spokesperson Felix Kwakye Ofosu that more than 200 filling stations, 11 fuel depots, two oil refineries, 33 factories and 12 public offices are now operating on a 24-hour basis under the government's 24-hour economy programme.
Mr Kwakye Ofosu says the initiative is boosting economic activity and creating jobs.
However, Mr Amoah argues that the government's claims of progress, including the reported 24-hour operations of filling stations, fuel depots, factories and public offices, do not reflect the original vision of the policy.
Speaking on Joy FM's Top Story on Thursday, November 19, Dr Amoah said the policy was intended to establish factories and industries capable of operating around the clock and creating employment opportunities for hundreds and thousands of Ghanaians.
He questioned the government's decision to count businesses and institutions that already operate around the clock as achievements under the initiative.
“Surprisingly, I think Felix Kwakye Ofosu, my own brother, is deceiving the public. We need to desist from some of these things as a country. We need to move beyond politics.
“The 24-hour economy they are talking about was basically about putting in place measures to ensure that we establish factories and industries that could employ hundreds or thousands of Ghanaians, so that they could earn three times... I'm surprised. I don't want to say he is lying, but I'm surprised. I mean, these are all political statements. I want to move beyond this. 24-hour economy that they meant we have not started. It's a fact," he said.
Dr Amoah also challenged claims surrounding a palm oil project expected to create 120,000 jobs, questioning the stage of implementation and how the projected employment figures had been determined.
He said his experience as a palm plantation farmer made him particularly interested in understanding the project's progress.
Dr Amoah urged the government to move beyond political claims and provide a clearer account of what it has achieved under the 24-hour economy programme.
